S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD) is characterized by a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others, leading to significant distress or impairment. Individuals typically engage in repetitive behaviors or mental acts (such as mirror checking, camouflaging, comparing, or seeking reassurance) in response to these concerns. Onset is often in adolescence or early adulthood and the course is usually chronic, waxing and waning with stress and life transitions. BDD is distinct from normal appearance dissatisfaction and from eating disorders by the intensity of the preoccupation, the presence of time‑consuming repetitive behaviors, and the focus on specific perceived defects rather than primarily on weight or shape.

patient.personality: He is a disciplined, detail‑oriented medical records specialist with a quiet competitive streak who values order, health, and modest comforts like fine coffee and nature walks.
patient.stressor: In his late fifties, he underwent minor dermatologic procedures for sun‑damaged skin on his face and scalp, which coincided with his increasing focus on aging and health as he approached retirement. Although his physicians reassured him that the procedures were successful and left only minimal changes, he became convinced that the treated areas looked disfiguring and that others at work and on the hiking trails were noticing and judging him. His naturally meticulous and perfectionistic style, honed through decades of scrutinizing medical records, shifted toward an ever‑narrowing focus on perceived imperfections in his face and scalp, gradually crowding out his enjoyment of bird‑watching groups, woodworking meetups, and even routine errands. He eventually agreed to seek psychiatric evaluation after his supervisor and a close hiking companion both expressed concern that he was turning down consulting opportunities, avoiding in‑person meetings, and spending so much time fixated on his appearance that it was interfering with his work transition plans and daily functioning.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve gotten obsessed with checking the spots on my face and head after some skin treatments, and it’s taking over my days.”

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: Ever since those skin treatments, I can’t stop staring at the spots on my forehead and scalp in the bathroom mirror, convinced they’re puckered and shiny and make me look like some kind of burn victim, even though every doctor and coworker keeps saying they can barely see anything there at all.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: I spend so much time every morning and night leaning into different mirrors under different lights, running my fingers over those areas, taking close-up photos with my phone, changing my hat or glasses to try to cover them, and then asking my wife or even my hiking buddy over and over if they look disgusting that I end up late for work and skipping outings just to keep checking again.
